findings.element: Evaluations list (landing) — rows with status "Fertig" but no "Anzeigen" button
findings.finding: Half the finished evaluations say they are done but offer no visible way to open them — no button, and the row name is not clickable either.
findings.user_impact: The user waits for a report, sees it marked finished, cannot find any way to read it, and concludes the tool is broken or that they did something wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Make every finished row openable (clickable row name plus the same "Anzeigen" button), and if a type genuinely has no viewable result, label it so — e.g. "Datei bereit" with a download action instead of "Fertig".

evidence.quote: only 9 of 28 rows have an 'Anzeigen' button. 10 of the 19 rows with status 'Fertig' have no way to open them at all (all Rohdaten Export, all Linienanalyse DPM, all Datenqualitätsindex rows). The row name is not clickable either (no onclick, cursor:auto) — a finished report of those types is a dead end.
evidence.source: state map → zone "evaluations list (landing)" → control "Open a finished evaluation"; plain-language principle: a status that says "done" must lead somewhere

findings.element: Wizard step 3 — "Run Now" button with the schedule box ticked, and the toast that follows
findings.finding: After setting up a repeating schedule and pressing Run Now, the only confirmation talks about a single run and the schedule never shows up in the scheduled list, so nothing confirms it was saved.
findings.user_impact: The user cannot tell whether the recurring report exists, so they either set it up a second time or stop trusting the schedule feature and go back to doing it by hand.
findings.suggested_fix: Say both things in the confirmation — e.g. "Evaluation started. Weekly schedule saved — view it under Geplante Berichte" — and link straight to the new schedule row.

evidence.quote: toast reads 'Evaluation started — running now' and the app returns to the list. Nothing in the confirmation mentions the schedule that was just configured, and the new schedule does not appear in Geplante Berichte. A user cannot tell whether the schedule was saved.
evidence.source: state map → zone "wizard step 3 — run" → control "Run Now (with the schedule box ticked)"; plain-language principle: missing reassurance that a saved setting was saved

findings.element: Type-selection cards and step-2 filter labels — "DPM", "(RPV)", "TU's", "(DQI)"
findings.finding: Four acronyms carry the whole meaning of the choose-a-report and choose-a-filter steps and none of them is expanded or explained anywhere on screen.
findings.user_impact: A newer or occasional user guesses which report type and which filter applies to them, picks the wrong one, and blames themselves rather than the label.
findings.suggested_fix: Expand each acronym once on first use and add a hover explanation — "DPM (Durchschnittliche Pünktlichkeitsmessung)", "RPV — Regionaler Personenverkehr", "TU — Transportunternehmen" — keeping the short form afterwards.

evidence.quote: Punctuality DPM, Raw Data Export DPM, Data Quality Index (DQI) DPM, Connection Punctuality, Trip Failures DPM, Line Analysis DPM
evidence.source: state map → zone "type selection" → control "6 report type cards", and zone "wizard step 2 — filters" labels "Transport Association (RPV)" and "TU's"; plain-language principle: unexplained acronym

gaps: Step-2 filter labels are recorded partly in German ("Kantone", "Linien", "Haltestellen", "Verkehrsmittel") and partly in English ("Transport Association", "TU's"), while the step-3 summary shows English ("Cantons:", "Lines:", "Stops:"). The map does not say which labels belong to the DE run and which to the EN run, so I cannot judge whether an English-language user meets untranslated German filter names.

Notify-by-email toggle + email input (step 3) is in not_exercised, so I cannot tell whether the user is ever reassured that they will be told when a long-running evaluation finishes — the main missing-reassurance risk after "Run Now".

No copy is recorded for what happens between "Run Now" and a finished report: no expected duration, no progress explanation, no statement of where the result will appear. A first-timer's biggest question after pressing the button is unanswered in the map.

The native delete confirm text is recorded, but not what the user is told they are losing (does deleting an evaluation also delete its schedule and any exported data?). I cannot assess the anxiety of that dialog without knowing the scope of the deletion.

Delete on an In-Progress row is disabled with the title still reading "Delete" and no explanation — recorded in the map but not reported here, as it fell below the 3-finding cap; worth picking up in a later round.
